t.7.63.1: Then, in the twelfth year, Śatrughna desired to go to Ayodhyā, which was protected by Rāma, followed by a small retinue of servants and troops.
t.7.63.2: Having sent back the ministers, the chief commanders of the army and the family priest, he went forth in a splendid, shining chariot, the foremost of chariots, yoked with horses.
t.7.63.4: Having entered the delightful city, that glorious, mighty-armed delight of the Ikṣvākus went in to where Rāma of great splendour was.
t.7.63.3: Having passed through just seven or eight halting-places, the delight of the Raghus swiftly went to Ayodhyā, eager to see Rāghava.
t.7.63.5: Having saluted the great-souled Rāma, who seemed to blaze with splendour and whose valour was true, he joined his palms in reverence and spoke to him.
t.7.63.6: O great king, all that you commanded I have done: that wicked Lavaṇa has been slain, and the city has been settled.
t.7.63.7: A twelfth year has passed without you, O Raghunandana; separated from you, O king, I cannot bear to live any longer.
t.7.63.9: Embracing Śatrughna, who was speaking thus, he said this: "Do not give way to despondency, O hero; this is not the conduct of a kṣatriya."
t.7.63.8: Therefore, O Kākutstha of boundless valor, grant me your favor, for without you I dwell far from home like a calf deprived of its mother.
t.7.63.10: Kings do not lose heart when dwelling far from home, O Rāghava, for the subjects must be protected according to the duty of a kṣatriya, O Rāghava.
t.7.63.11: From time to time, O hero, come to Ayodhyā to see me, O best of men, and then you shall go back to your own city.
t.7.63.12: You too are most dear to me, dearer even than my life breaths; of that there is no doubt. Yet the protection of the kingdom must necessarily be carried out.
t.7.63.13: Therefore, O Kākutstha, stay here with me for five nights; after that you shall go to Madhurā with your servants, your army and your mounts.
t.7.63.14: Hearing these words of Rāma, righteous and pleasing to the mind, Śatrughna replied in a sorrowful voice, saying only, "So be it."
t.7.63.15: Having stayed there for five nights in accordance with the command of Rāghava, that great archer Kākutstha then prepared to depart.
t.7.63.16: Having taken leave of the great-souled Rāma, whose valour was true, and of Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa as well, he mounted his great chariot.
t.7.63.17: Accompanied for a long way by those two, the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, Śatrughna then went swiftly to the city.
